note: #3126 (seat:caa's rulings of 2026-09-27 on #3126; research 0031 rows 3 and 5): a theory that STOPPED before it decided a ground literal is NOT DECIDED, never false, and check refuses it by name (builtin_not_decided) in every position: a Builtin node, a support edge's builtin, and a closure rule instance whose body is not decided and whose head is absent. The stop is the decimal alignment work cap: two in-domain decimals whose exponents differ by more than MAX_DECIMAL_SCALE_SHIFT (65,536). Each refused case is paired with a control that is decided. Hand-authored from the spec (logos-contract.md 5, decide_ground) and the ruling; no case was captured from a run. Driven through every core's conformance CLI as the negation family (conformance/harness.mjs, cli: negation), so the notation, the negation_v1 profile and the context binding are negation.json's; the negation_v1 profile's theory carries the standard arithmetic theory beside lt since #3126. An int is Tuple[Atom(int), Atom(sign byte + big-endian magnitude)] (atom = hex bytes), a decimal is decimal(int(m), int(e)) = m x 10^e, and an operator compound is Tuple[Atom(op), ...].

cases.name: closure_filter_past_the_work_cap_is_not_decided
cases.note: THE RED-FIRST WITNESS. q_cap :- 10^60000 + 10^-60000 > 1. r_cap :- \+ q_cap. The certificate seals q_cap EMPTY. The comparison HOLDS (the sum exceeds 1), so q_cap is true and the certificate omits a true fact. The two operands are in ADR 0022's value domain, and aligning them needs a shift of 120,000 > MAX_DECIMAL_SCALE_SHIFT (65,536): a work cap, the value exists and was not computed. Until #3126 every core read the stop as Fails, so the closure saw a false body, asked for no head, and check ACCEPTED r_cap, certifying \+ q_cap while q_cap holds. The closure now reads the literal NOT DECIDED, and a rule instance whose body is not decided and whose head is absent is refused builtin_not_decided.

cases.name: closure_filter_in_bound_holds_control
cases.note: The control of closure_filter_past_the_work_cap_is_not_decided with a gap of 12: 10^6 + 10^-6 > 1 is DECIDED true, so the closure requires q_holds, and a certificate sealing it empty is not closed.

cases.name: closure_filter_in_bound_fails_control
cases.note: The accepted control: 10^6 + 10^-6 < 1 is DECIDED false, so the rule instance holds with q_fails absent, the certificate is closed, and \+ q_fails is certified.

cases.name: closure_absorbs_a_stop_by_a_later_false_literal
cases.note: q_cap_then_false :- 10^60000 + 10^-60000 > 1, 1 < 0. The first literal is not decided (the work cap, a literal-scoped stop) and the second is DECIDED false, so the body is false (F and U is F) and the instance holds with the head absent: accepted. A stop is refused only where no decided false absorbs it.

cases.name: closure_prunes_at_a_false_literal_before_the_stop
cases.note: q_false_then_cap :- 1 < 0, 10^60000 + 10^-60000 > 1. The first literal is DECIDED false, so the body is false whatever the second is, and the closure prunes there: accepted, the order-swapped twin of closure_absorbs_a_stop_by_a_later_false_literal.

cases.name: closure_negated_filter_past_the_work_cap_is_not_decided
cases.note: seat:caa's named witness: q_neg_cap :- \+ (10^60000 + 10^-60000 =:= 1). A negation of a literal that is not decided is not decided (not(U) = U), so with q_neg_cap sealed empty the instance's truth is not established: refused builtin_not_decided. (Until #3126 the stop read Fails, the negation read true, and this was refused cert_not_closed, under a name that claimed a violation nobody had shown.)

cases.name: support_builtin_past_the_work_cap_is_not_decided
cases.note: q_cap_held :- 10^60000 + 10^-60000 > 1, sealed WITH q_cap_held and a support edge whose builtin body ref is that comparison; the ref's arguments are in the certificate's domain (spec 3.4), so the support check is reached. The closure holds through the present head, and the support check must decide the builtin: not decided, refused builtin_not_decided. Until #3126 the stop read Fails and this was refused cert_unsupported ('does not hold'). Its control is support_builtin_in_bound_holds_control.

cases.name: support_builtin_in_bound_holds_control
cases.note: The control for support_builtin_past_the_work_cap_is_not_decided: the same shape over q_holds, whose comparison is in bound and holds. The certificate is valid (the support check decides the builtin ref and it holds), so check reaches the negation premise (ADR 0007 section 4, step 6 after step 2): q_holds IS sealed present, so \+ q_holds is refused neg_atom_present. It passes before and after #3126, and it fails if the support check is never reached (an argument outside the domain would read cert_out_of_domain).

cases.name: builtin_node_past_the_work_cap_is_not_decided
cases.note: A derivation whose root is the Builtin node 10^60000 + 10^-60000 > 1. The comparison holds and was not decided: refused builtin_not_decided (until #3126 it was refused builtin_failed, a decided false that is untrue).

cases.name: builtin_node_in_bound_control
cases.note: The control with a gap of 12: 10^6 + 10^-6 > 1 is decided and holds, so the Builtin node is accepted.

cases.name: builtin_node_in_bound_false_control
cases.note: The false control with a gap of 12: 10^6 + 10^-6 =\= 1000000.000001 is decided and does not hold, so the Builtin node is refused builtin_failed, a completed decision.
